cases.title: Tenant schedules and executes reliable background work
cases.goal: A tenant schedules idempotent work and the system executes it with bounded retries.

mainFlow.action: The tenant enqueues immediate or recurring work.
The scheduler materializes due schedules and a worker claims and executes jobs.

acceptanceCriteria: Every job remains tenant-owned, idempotency keys suppress duplicates, and exhausted retries enter the dead-letter state.

cases.title: Mobile member works offline and safely synchronizes
cases.goal: A mobile member reserves identifiers, records offline mutations, and synchronizes them after connectivity returns.

mainFlow.action: The client validates the session and device posture before opening local storage.
The client reserves numbering, records a mutation, and synchronizes the queued change.

acceptanceCriteria: Tenant and device context bind every local mutation, and conflicts require explicit resolution rather than silent overwrite.

cases.title: Tenant sends preference-aware notifications
cases.goal: A tenant queues a notification that is rendered, dispatched, and visible in the recipient inbox without leaking PII.

mainFlow.action: The tenant queues a template-backed notification for a recipient.
A worker dispatches due deliveries and the recipient reads the in-app item.

acceptanceCriteria: Opt-outs are honored, delivery transitions are auditable, and logs contain identifiers rather than rendered PII.

cases.title: Offline client reserves numbers and resolves synchronization conflicts
cases.goal: An authenticated tenant client reserves numbering, submits a sync batch, and explicitly resolves any conflict.

mainFlow.action: The client reserves and, when necessary, cancels an unused numbering interval.
The client submits a batch and explicitly resolves a reported conflict.

acceptanceCriteria: All four operations require tenant context, permission checks, and audit events; a conflict is never silently overwritten.

cases.title: Domain write produces a reliably acknowledged integration event
cases.goal: A domain transaction emits an outbox message that is dispatched and acknowledged without losing tenant identity.

mainFlow.action: The domain write enqueues its event in the same database transaction.
A worker claims and dispatches the message; the receiver returns a signed acknowledgement.

acceptanceCriteria: The domain write and enqueue commit atomically, retries are bounded, and ambiguous or invalid acknowledgements fail closed.

cases.title: Supervisor manages a tenant work queue from enqueue to completion
cases.goal: A tenant creates a governed queue, assigns eligible work, completes it, and detects SLA breaches.

mainFlow.action: A supervisor creates a queue and a member enqueues a tenant work item.
An eligible member claims and completes the item.
The system detects overdue open work and records breach events.

acceptanceCriteria: RLS, RBAC eligibility, assignment ownership, supervisor overrides, and the append-only event history remain enforced.
